definition: Pax Silica (Latin for 'Silicon Peace') is a United States-led international initiative focused on securing supply chains for advanced technologies such as semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), and rare earth elements.
details: The initiative implicitly targets reducing reliance on China and countering its dominance in these fields. The initiative is coordinated by the U.S. Department of State and was launched in December 2025 alongside the signing of the non-binding Pax Silica Declaration by an initial group of partner countries. It is the U.S.-led counterpart to the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization.

explainer.lead: A United States-led international initiative to secure supply chains for advanced technologies such as semiconductors, AI and rare earth elements. It implicitly aims to reduce reliance on China and counter its dominance in these fields.

tiers.eli5: It is a group of countries agreeing to work together so the key parts for computers and AI do not all come from one supplier.
tiers.practitioner: The initiative is coordinated by the U.S. Department of State and was launched in December 2025 with an initial group of partner countries signing the non-binding Pax Silica Declaration. Being non-binding and new, it offers a diplomatic framework rather than enforceable rules.

explainer.example: An initial group of partner countries signs the non-binding Pax Silica Declaration in December 2025, committing to cooperate on securing semiconductor and rare earth supply chains.
